newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico conservatives to win northern state - poll.
newsitem.headline: Mexico conservatives to win northern state - poll.

text.p: Mexico's right-wing National Action Party (PAN) has dealt President Ernesto Zedillo's party a crushing defeat in the governorship for key northern industrial state Nuevo Leon, a TV Azteca exit poll said on Sunday.

The poll showed the PAN's Fernando Canales Clariond with 42 percent of the vote, way ahead of the ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI). Their candidate, former Deputy Interior Minister Jose Natividad Gonzalez Paras trailed with just 28 percent.
If official preliminary results later on Sunday night confirm the poll, it would mean a grave defeat for the PRI, which had claimed the race was neck-and-neck with the PAN.
Nuevo Leon's capital Monterrey is the nation's second largest industrial centre and Mexico's third largest city, with a population of more than two million.

Preliminary official results are scheduled to be released at about 2100 local (0200 GMT). The Nuevo Leon race is the most important of six governor's races being decided on Sunday. Mexicans were also electing a mayor of Mexico City, a new lower house of congress and a quarter of the Senate.
